name: Knockgrafton

attributes.attribute: mountain in the Glen of Aherlow
sang a song of Monday, Tuesday
extended the fairy song with wit

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Knockgrafton is an Irish mythological site. It sits at the foot of the Galtee range within the Aherlow glen. On this mountain a hunchback heard fairies singing a dull song. Their tune ran only Monday, Tuesday. His sharp mind let him add to the fairy song. The fairies were pleased with his skill. They cured his bent back. The same tale shows up across the Celtic lands.

okr.objective: Knockgrafton is where a witty hunchback earned a cure from fairies.
key_results: Knockgrafton is an Irish mythological site.
It lies in the Glen of Aherlow below the Galtee Mountains.
There fairies sang a dull song of Monday, Tuesday.
A hunchback added words and the fairies cured him.
